description: Golden cases for app/services/memory_extraction.py::extract_signals. Add a case any time a real conversation reveals a false-positive or false-negative. The runner asserts each `expected.<field>` matches one of: 'empty', 'fires', or a substring the title/rule must contain.

cases.prev_assistant: Take a break, you need it!
cases.notes: Speaker-flip: Daniel venting AT Gooni, not directing tone. No instruction phrase = no rule.

cases.text: Are you able to add to my calendar?
cases.prev_assistant: You're free tomorrow, so it looks like you can fit in tennis!
cases.notes: Capability question — must hit hard gate, not auto-log feature.

cases.text: Do you have the ability to log focused?
cases.prev_assistant: How are you feeling about that?
cases.notes: Capability question — was previously slipping through prompt's example list, now caught by hard gate.

cases.prev_assistant: Your current focuses are getting a startup job.
cases.notes: User-side capability question (not 'can you' but 'can I'). Same intent.
Polite-imperative shape that English speakers use to mean 'please add X'. Hard gate treats as question. If the right behavior is to fire here, this case will need to flip.

cases.text: stop using filler like "happy to help"
cases.prev_assistant: I'd be happy to help with that!
cases.notes: Explicit instruction phrase + grounded evidence — must fire.
Plain imperative — must fire. Title should contain 'calendar' or similar.

cases.text: you should be able to set timers
Can you X? Just add it.
cases.notes: Question + same-message follow-up imperative. Hard gate's only documented exception. Imperative trumps question.
